title: introduce-token-stapling-and-lightweight-resume-adapters-across-sdks
author: Anjali Kapoor
release_notes: Adds token stapling and resume adapter helpers to Python/TS/Go SDKs; improves streaming resume reliability for short-lived credentials; bump minor versions for all SDKs.
description:
Context and motivation: Several customers and internal integrations were losing in-flight streaming sessions when short-lived delegated credentials rotated during long-lived streaming operations. Existing SDKs had ad-hoc retry and resume helpers in individual languages; this PR converges on a lightweight, cross-language pattern we call "token stapling" plus a small "resume adapter" to improve developer ergonomics and reduce duplicate work.
Goals: (1) ensure in-flight streams can be resumed without re-running the entire prompt when a credential swap occurs, (2) provide a small, idiomatic helper surface for Python/TypeScript/Go that is easy to adopt, (3) centralize telemetry points for resume/reconnect so telemetry and SRE can reason about session churn.
Summary of changes: - Add token-staple middleware and resume adapter in each SDK (ts: src/stream/tokenStaple.ts, py: redwood/stream/token_staple.py, go: stream/token_staple.go). The implementation is intentionally minimal: it attaches a short-lived credential footprint (staple) to stream requests and knows how to rehydrate that staple during a resumed session.
- Introduce ResumeMarker protocol/wire-contract (opaque string marker saved by client consumer) and ResumeAdapter class to glue stapling + incremental resume logic.
- Implement a small client-side warmup hook that prefetches a 1-request heartbeat using the stapled token so the server can prime KV cache and reduce first-token latency after resume. This is optional and off by default.
- Add typed examples for all three SDKs showing how to convert existing streaming consumers to the new adapter surface.
- Add tests (unit + integration harness) and new telemetry counters: sdk.stream.resume.attempt, sdk.stream.resume.success, sdk.stream.resume.failure, sdk.stream.staple.refresh.
- Bump versions: ts SDK to 1.14.0, py SDK to 0.18.0, go SDK to v1.9.0.
Commits (high level): - 7f2c9a2: introduce token staple core and tests (ts) - b1e8d33: python port + examples - c3a5f77: go port + CI matrix adjustment - e9f4d12: add resume marker contract and docs - 35d9c00: telemetry counters and metrics docs - f2a1b21: examples and release notes
Changes by area (selected files): - src/stream/tokenStaple.ts: new middleware class TokenStaple that wraps fetch/stream handshake, attaches staple metadata header, and exposes refresh(token) helper.
- src/stream/resumeAdapter.ts: new high-level adapter that exposes start(), onResume(marker), close().
- examples/ts/streaming-resume.md: new quickstart showing common migration path.
- redwood/stream/token_staple.py: Python analog with contextmanager-friendly API.
- go/stream/token_staple.go: Go implementation using context.Context for cancellation.
- sdk-integration-tests/stream-resume-harness: adds a small harness that simulates short-lived token rotation and validates resume counters.
- docs/streaming/upgrade-guide.md: explains the pattern and recommended safety checks.
Testing and CI: CI matrix was updated to run the stream resume harness in the integration stage for Python and TypeScript; Go unit tests added to the existing Go CI workflow. All checks passed on the final run.
Notes about compatibility and ergonomics: - The token stapling layer is opt-in; existing consumers continue to function unchanged. To adopt: wrap your stream consumer with ResumeAdapter and pass a stapled token obtained from your credential pipeline.
- Resume markers are opaque to the SDK (string). They are saved externally by the application (e.g., user session store) and passed back to the SDK when attempting resume.
- The warmup hook should be used only for latency-sensitive windows; it creates a short burst (1 request) and therefore impacts billing minimally.
Review summary and conversation: - Marco Li (reviewer): "Nice convergence. Two asks: (1) can we make the telemetry tags include deployment id? (2) add a test that simulates multi-tenant token swaps." Response (Anjali): "Added deployment_id tag to all resume metrics and added a multi-tenant simulation test in the harness. Test is non-flaky under CI matrix." - Priya Nair: "API surface looks clean. Suggest renaming `onResume` -> `resumeFromMarker` for explicitness." Response: "Renamed to resume_from_marker() in Python/Go and resumeFromMarker in TS; updated docs/examples." - Ethan Morales: "Please document the interaction with existing backoff/retry profiles so customers don't double-retry during resume." Response: "Expanded section in docs/streaming/upgrade-guide.md describing how ResumeAdapter cooperates with SDK retry presets; default behavior is to suppress backoff during resume handshake for a configurable window." - Follow-ups: small linter fixes, updated examples to TypeScript async-iterator patterns, and tidied Go documentation comments. CI summary: - Unit tests (ts, py, go): pass - Integration harness (stream-resume-harness): pass - Linting: pass - Coverage: unchanged (+0.2% in ts) Migration and rollout plan: - This PR is opt-in; we will publish new minor SDK releases and call out the resume ergonomics in the changelogs.
- We will enable the integration harness in nightly runs for two weeks to capture early failures.
- SRE will subscribe to new telemetry and create a dashboard to monitor resume success rates and latency regressions.
Docs and examples: - Added a short migration guide and three inline examples showing the minimal changes required to adopt the resume adapter across languages.
Release note blurb (for changelog): "SDKs: add optional token stapling and resume adapters to improve in-flight stream resilience when short-lived credentials rotate. See streaming/upgrade-guide for details." Potential risks and mitigations: - Risk: apps storing resume markers incorrectly could leak session state; mitigation: docs emphasize markers are opaque and should be scoped per-user.
- Risk: warmup hook increases billing slightly; mitigation: off by default and documented.
Overall: converges three SDK implementations on a small cross-language pattern that reduces duplication for customers, improves streaming reliability during credential rotation, and keeps the runtime/server contract minimal.
